rulings.rationale: Before creating a presentation, the artifacts commit to detecting the infrastructure, choosing where it goes and scaffolding what is missing. They do not commit to doing this before modifying a presentation. The modification scenario covers only editing, keeping the presentation registered and running the self-check. The phrase 'the same rules' points to the authoring rules (scene reuse, scene groups, stable ids, registration), not to detection and setup. This matches the item's partial anchor: bootstrapping runs on create but not on modify.
evidence: The authoring workflow (spec lines 13-17) runs in this order for a topic: outline, detect the target project, set it up, then author and register. Setup by project type (lines 45-54) and the design's per-role path binding in plan.ts (design lines 240-256) cover detection, deciding where pieces go, and scaffolding only the missing ones.

The Presentation authoring requirement says 'Modifying an existing presentation SHALL follow the same rules and self-check'. Its scenario (spec lines 191-193) says only that the skill edits the presentation, keeps it registered and runs its self-check. Neither says detection or scaffolding happens before a modification.

rulings.rationale: Setup installs the missing runtime, build and verification packages with the project's package manager instead of assuming they exist. The skill itself installs the matching browser after the user confirms. The chosen self-check has no lint step, so this implementation needs no linting dependencies.
evidence: The design's dependency list (lines 263-265) adds whichever are missing: react, react-dom, motion and lucide-react, plus dev dependencies vite, @vitejs/plugin-react, typescript, the type packages and @playwright/test@1.61.0. apply.ts runs the detected package manager's install (lines 269-273).

The spec says dependencies are installed with the lockfile's package manager (lines 51-52). It also says a missing browser is reported as a provisioning problem and that the skill installs a browser after user confirmation (lines 200-201). The proposal says the same at lines 140-141.

rulings.rationale: The resources are said to ship with the skill, and the scripts run from the skill directory with the target passed separately. No artifact says how the scripts locate their bundled templates independently of the working directory. 'Invoked from the skill directory' is an invocation convention, not a resolution rule. This matches the partial anchor: the resources ship with the skill, but how the skill finds them is not stated.
evidence: The spec requires the skill to bundle the scene kit, app template and harness so it works without this repository (lines 3-11). The design lists them under skills/presentation/assets (lines 41-58).

The design says scripts are 'invoked from the skill directory with --target <dir>' (lines 217-219). I found no statement in the spec, design or proposal that template paths are resolved relative to the skill file or the script's own location.

rulings.rationale: Each presentation is its own unit: its own files under a bound presentations directory, with a unique slug. It is registered in the index and reachable at its own route. Adding one creates only presentation files and an index registration, so it does not interfere with other presentations.
evidence: The authoring scenario (spec lines 19-22) requires the new presentation to be registered in the index and reachable at its own route. The index requirement (scene-presentation lines 215-222) makes every registered presentation reachable at its own route.

The design binds a presentationsDir role (lines 244-245). Its layout shows a presentation in its own folder with scenes.tsx and index.ts, plus a registry entry (lines 62-63). The second-run scenario (spec lines 134-137) limits changes to presentation files and the index registration.

rulings.rationale: The artifacts say existing files are never overwritten and every registered presentation is reachable at its own route. No requirement or scenario says that creating a new presentation keeps the earlier presentations registered in the index and still reachable. The index registration is itself changed when a presentation is added, and its effect on existing entries is not stated.
evidence: The confirmation requirement says the skill never overwrites an existing file it does not intend to merge into (spec lines 147-150). The second-run scenario changes only presentation files and the index registration (lines 134-137).

The index requirement (scene-presentation lines 215-222) lists every registered presentation and makes each reachable. No scenario says earlier registrations survive when a new presentation is created.

checks.rationale: The dissent is right about what the design says. Step 6 of `verify.ts` (design.md lines 310–312) says to print each failure, stop the preview server, and then exit 1 if any failure or error was collected, otherwise 0. So stopping the server is a committed step on both exit paths, including runs that fail. That matches the item's requirement that started preview processes are cleaned up after each run, including failed runs. It goes beyond the partial anchor, which applies when cleanup is stated only for the normal path. Type-check, build and argument failures exit before the preview starts in step 3, so nothing is left running in those cases. The design does not mention the server explicitly on the step-4 early exit (manifest absent), but that does not cancel the explicit failure-path cleanup the requirement looks for.
evidence: design.md lines 310–311: "Print each failure as `step / mode / viewport / message`, stop the preview server, and exit 1 if any failure or error was collected, otherwise 0." Cleanup comes be…
design.md lines 296–298: type-check and build failures "exit 1 without starting a browser" before step 3 starts `vite preview`, so those failing runs start no preview process.

results.rationale: The verify command is committed to type-check and build the whole app and to fail unsuccessfully when the build fails. The design names the mechanism: local tsc, then vite build, with exit 1 on either failure.
evidence: The Repository verify command requirement says the command 'type-checks and builds the whole app' and exits unsuccessfully otherwise.
The 'Build failure' and 'Type error fails verification' scenarios require an unsuccessful exit with no browser run.
design.md verify step 2 runs the project's local tsc and then vite build, and on either failure prints the output and exits 1.

results.rationale: Verification confirms the sample slug is registered and reachable and steps through every step. It does not commit to checking the sample's steps against an expected outline. Titles are compared with the manifest, which comes from the same definition, and no spec or design text states an expected ordered step list for verification.
evidence: design.md verify step 4 reports a slug missing from the manifest as 'not registered', which covers presence and reachability.
design.md verify step 5 asserts marker i / N, the manifest title and at least one entity per step. The expected titles come from the presentation's own manifest, not an independent outline.
The registered-presentation unit test only runs the structure check, and the 'Sample covers the workflow' scenario is not tied to a verification gate.

results.rationale: The verify command targets the named sample slug. A slug missing from the manifest is reported as not registered, and any collected failure exits 1. A deleted sample or registration also breaks the type-check or build, which exits 1.
evidence: design.md verify step 4: 'if the slug is not in the manifest, report it as not registered'.
design.md step 6 exits 1 if any failure was collected, and steps 2 and 3 fail on type or build errors.
The package script runs verify with --slug using-the-presentation-skill, so it cannot pass vacuously over an empty registry.

results.rationale: The spec and design commit verification to a real Playwright Chromium run against vite preview of the production build. It steps through every step in both modes and fails on console errors, page errors and unhandled rejections.
evidence: The Repository verify command requirement says it 'serves its production preview' and drives a real browser through every step in both modes at desktop and phone viewports.
The Error gate requirement fails on console errors, uncaught errors and unhandled rejections.
design.md verify steps 3 to 5 start vite preview and collect console error and pageerror events across all steps.

results.rationale: Console errors, uncaught errors, navigation failures and render failures each fail verification, and failures are reported with step, mode, viewport and message.
evidence: The Error gate scenarios fail the check for a console error at step 3 and an uncaught error at step 5, reporting each with its step.
The Functional gate scenarios fail 'Wrong step after navigation' at step 3 and 'Blank diagram' at step 2.
design.md prints each failure as 'step / mode / viewport / message', and the harness fixtures include a thrown error.

results.rationale: The outcome is unambiguous: exit 0 on success and distinct non-zero codes (1, 2, 64) otherwise. Failures are reported with step, mode, viewport and message, and the type-check, build and browser stages are reported separately.
evidence: The Repository verify command requirement says it succeeds only when every check passes, otherwise exits unsuccessfully and reports each failure.
design.md steps 2 and 6 define exit 1 for type, build and browser failures, exit 2 for provisioning, exit 64 for invalid arguments, and exit 0 otherwise.
The Failure is located scenario requires the report to identify the step, mode, viewport and failed check.

results.rationale: The design stops the preview server at the end of the normal and failure-collecting flow. It does not commit to cleanup for aborted or early-exit runs, and neither the spec nor the test plan asserts it.
evidence: design.md verify step 6 says 'Print each failure..., stop the preview server, and exit 1 if any failure or error was collected', which covers failures collected in the normal flow.
Step 4 exits 1 immediately for a missing verification protocol, with no statement that the preview server is stopped.
No spec scenario or test-plan assertion (INT-004) checks that preview processes are cleaned up after a failing or aborted run.

results.rationale: The harness ships a scripted screenshot helper, installed into projects as the presentation:screenshots script. It captures every step at 1440×900 by default and writes to a predictable git-ignored directory.
evidence: The Screenshot helper requirement captures each step in both modes at 1440 × 900 by default and writes to a git-ignored directory with names identifying presentation, step, mode and viewport.
design.md screenshot.ts shares the preview and build flow and writes presentation-screenshots/<slug>/<slug>-step-<NN>-<mode>-<desktop|phone>.png.
Setup adds the presentation:screenshots script to target projects.

results.rationale: The screenshot helper waits for the Stage's settle signal, a fixed-timer data-animating flag, before each capture. It also uses reduced motion, so captures show settled states.
evidence: design.md screenshot.ts 'navigates directly to each step URL, waits for the settle signal', and uses reducedMotion: 'reduce'.
design.md defines the settle signal: data-animating returns to 'false' SETTLE_MS after each step change, so the wait is tied to transition completion.

votes.rationale: The skill is defined as an agent procedure (SKILL.md plus references) backed by bundled reusable infrastructure: a canonical scene kit, app template, page-entry assets, a verification harness, and setup scripts. Output quality is checked by defined gates: a structure check, type-check, build, browser check with error and functional gates, and a screenshot review checklist. This is not prompt-only generation.
evidence: design.md lays out SKILL.md (workflow, confirmation and retry rules, commands, report format), references, assets (scene-kit, harness, app-template, page-entry) and scripts (detect/plan/apply).
The presentation-skill spec requires a self-check (structure check, build, browser check, up to three fix attempts) and a screenshot review that fixes overlap and clipping.
The scene kit exposes `checkPresentation`, and the harness runs verify.ts as the quality gate on generated output.

votes.rationale: The design commits to one documented entry point, `npm run verify`, backed by `verify.ts`. It type-checks, builds the whole app, serves the preview, and steps a real browser through every step of the sample in both modes. The spec requires it to exit unsuccessfully on any failure.
evidence: The presentation-verification spec's 'Repository verify command' requirement says it type-checks and builds the whole app, serves the preview, and drives a real browser through every step in both modes.
design.md Repository tooling defines the package.json script `verify` as `node scripts/presentation/verify.ts --slug using-the-presentation-skill`.
verify.ts's steps are type-check, then build, then preview, then browser steps, all in one script.

votes.rationale: The design and spec commit the render check to real Chromium, driven by the Playwright library against a production `vite preview` of the built output. The jsdom tests are used only for unit-level checks, not as the render check. Real animation is exercised: the harness waits on the settle signal rather than stubbing it.
evidence: The verification spec says the verify command 'drives a real browser' against the 'production preview'.
design.md describes verify.ts using `chromium.executablePath()`, `vite build` and `vite preview`, and fresh browser contexts at 1440×900 and 390×844.
The harness waits on `data-animating="false"` rather than disabling animation.

votes.rationale: The design commits the viewer to a documented verification protocol that external tooling reads. `window.__presentationManifest` lists each presentation's steps, so the total is available. `data-step` and `data-mode` sit on the viewer root, and `data-entity-id` and `data-animating` give further hooks. The harness uses the manifest and these attributes rather than counting navigation markup, and reports a distinct error when the protocol is missing.
evidence: design.md's scene kit contract lists the verification protocol: `window.__presentationManifest`, `data-mode` and `data-step` on the viewer root, `data-entity-id` on each entity, and `data-animating` on the Stage.
The manifest shape is `[{ slug, title, steps: [{ title }] }]`, which gives the total step count; `data-step` gives the current index.
verify.ts reads the manifest for the slug and reports 'scene kit does not implement the verification protocol' when it is absent; the verification spec requires this.

The most process-like scenarios still name checkable results. 'Overlap is fixed' ends in the skill adjusting the presentation, re-running the self-check, and re-reviewing the affected step. 'Skill used outside this repository' ends in a working app and presentation built from bundled assets. 'Sample covers the workflow' lists the topics the steps must cover.

Looser wording, such as 'visibly marked as the focus' for emphasis and 'animates from' for transitions, is paired with an observable condition (marked on step 3 and not on step 4; the settled diagram equals the target).

votes.rationale: I found no concrete fact where the design contradicts a specification. Sizes, counts, names, keys, thresholds, and behaviors agree wherever both artifacts address them.
evidence: Compared the design with the specs on fixed values. The 60-character title limit, the 1440 × 900 and 390 × 844 viewports, the 1024 px table-of-contents breakpoint, the left-third tap zone, and the key sets (Right/Down/Space/PageDown, Home/End, P, Escape) all match.

Compared setup behavior. The design sends a monorepo to `presentations/`, reuses the page and config on a second run, treats blockers as unoverridable by `--confirmed`, and appends the two `.gitignore` entries. The skill spec says the same.

Compared verification behavior. The design runs the preflight first, skips the browser on type or build failure, and reports the 'scene kit does not implement the verification protocol' message. The verification spec matches.
The design routes standalone projects to the `page-entry` variant. The spec only says to 'scaffold at the project root, merging', so this is added detail, not a contradiction.

votes.rationale: The test plan's setups and expected results agree with the specs on counts, sizes, paths, and behaviors. I found no contradiction.
evidence: INT-004 expects 16 default screenshots at 1440 × 900 and exactly 2 selected ones at 390 × 844. This matches the screenshot-helper spec scenarios.

E2E-002 expects the table of contents only at widths of 1024 px or more, and no horizontal scrolling at the listed sizes. It expects opening mode to follow URL, then declared mode, then browse. The viewer spec says the same.

E2E-001 uses viewports of 1440 × 900 and 390 × 844. INT-003 expects verify to exit 1 with the missing-protocol message and no step failures. INT-002 expects `apply --confirmed` on a plan with blockers to write nothing. All match the specs.
The plan names exit codes 2 and 64, which the specs leave open. This is added detail, not a contradiction.

votes.rationale: Every entry under Decisions gives a reason with the choice, except possibly the last one, which has a looser reason. At most one decision lacks a reason.
evidence: Registry Stage: chosen over `layoutId` because `layoutId` targets HTML boxes and not SVG under a scaled viewBox. The entry also names the trade-off.
SVG with viewBox: 'gives uniform, uncropped scaling for free'. Hash routing: 'works on static hosting... cannot collide with a host router'.

Separate page entry: 'leaves host configuration untouched; the cost is separate scripts'. Plan/apply split: 'keeps detection and planning pure and testable, and makes the confirmation rule enforceable'.
Playwright library: 'to control exit codes'. Node type stripping: 'to match erasableSyntaxOnly and avoid a build step'.
Canonical assets plus drift test: the rationale is the distinction between this repository and other projects. It is less explicit but still states a purpose.

votes.rationale: Every requirement has a planned check. Most appear in the coverage map. The rest are assigned to unit tests or to the agent-executed acceptance run.
evidence: The coverage map lists the viewer requirements (routes, URL state, opening mode, present and browse modes, navigation, mode switching, responsive layout, reduced motion). It also lists most scene-presentation requirements, the skill requirements for detection through confirmation, the verification gates, preflight, screenshot helper, and bootstrap.

Presentation definition, Structure check, and the Unit test gate are not in the map. The plan says specs are the source of unit-test requirements and lists 'every structure-check problem code', the drift check, and the registered-presentation check as unit tests.

Presentation authoring, Authoring workflow, Self-check, Screenshot review, and Outcome report are not in the map. The Acceptance Testing Envelope plans an agent-executed run of the skill. It covers authoring a topic, modifying a presentation, breaking a presentation to exercise the fix attempts and failure report, and screenshot review. It names the outcome report as a risk area to check.
